newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan says no plans to buy more U.S. wheat.
newsitem.headline: Japan says no plans to buy more U.S. wheat.

text.p: Japan's Food Agency said on Wednesday that it has no immediate plans to resort to buying more U.S. wheat despite serious shipping delays at Canadian ports.

"We're closely monitoring shipments of Canadian wheat which have been delayed. But Japan currently has domestic wheat stocks equal to national consumption for 2.5 months," the Food Agency's trade division director Shinichi Yahagi told Reuters.
"We have no immediate plans to buy more U.S. wheat despite the shipment problem in Canada," Yahagi said.
The Chicago Board of Trade's (CBOT) wheat futures soared on Tuesday due to serious shipping delays at Canadian ports that could force buyers to turn to the United States.
About 1.5 million tonnes of Canadian wheat shipments have been delayed since January due to severe winter weather, and February and March shipments may be postponed as well.
"We're ready to release some domestic stocks amid delays in the arrival of Canadian wheat," Yahagi said.
The Food Agency, the grain trading arm of the Agriculture Ministry, is Japan's sole importer of wheat, barley and rice.
The agency is a major buyer of Canadian wheat 1CW, which is mainly used here for making bread.
